papers.title: Electronic structure and elasticity of the Ta-W solid solution
papers.abstract: The brittleness or ductility of metals has long been attributed to their elastic constants, with high Poisson ratio, or equivalently high Pugh ratio, favoring greater ductility. Growing evidence links ductility with their electronic structure. Consequently, it is desirable to understand how the electronic structure affects the elastic constants. Here, we examine the Ta-W binary alloy system, which evolves from ductile character at Ta-rich compositions to brittleness at high W. We show that a change in slope of the composition-dependent shear modulus near the equiatomic composition coincides with an abrupt change in the Fermi level density of states. We relate the behaviors of the elastic constants to the characters of occupied electronic orbitals close to the Fermi level. Finally, we consider additional alloy systems from groups V and VI and show that qualitatively similar behavior occurs more broadly.

summary_en.motivation: To understand how electronic structure governs the ductile-to-brittle transition in Ta-W binary alloys.
summary_en.method: First-principles calculations were performed to compute elastic constants and electronic density of states across compositions.
summary_en.result: A slope change in shear modulus near equiatomic composition correlates with an abrupt change in Fermi-level density of states.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical validation through comparison of elastic constant trends and electronic orbital analysis.
